text:
maya: Quick FYI — I'm kicking off an adaptive-reservoir canary for int4-v3 across 5% of prod traffic right now. goal: catch reranker regressions and prefix hallucination spikes before wider promote.

oliver: Nice. what's the gating signal? exact metrics?

maya: Primary gates: +0.8% top1 precision drop on rerank benchmark OR +1.0% delta in hallucination-rate proxy (response-entity-mismatch). Secondary: 99p latency <= baseline+40ms. If either primary trips, auto-fallback to nf4-v2.

rachel: Can you paste the config? want to run the offline check on our eval slices.

maya: ```
canary:
  variant: int4-v3
  traffic_pct: 5
  gates:
    rerank_precision_delta: -0.008
    hallucination_delta: 0.01
    latency_tail_ms: 40
  window: 30m
  min_samples: 500
  reservoir_sampling: true
  reservoir_size: 10000
  auto_fallback: true
  fallback_variant: nf4-v2
  alert: "#eng-ml"
```

jd: reservoir_sampling=true is interesting — how are we stratifying? user buckets? route?

maya: Stratified by route + client_tier so we avoid noisy tiny clients. reservoir fills uniformly across slices, we also force 20% of samples from traffic with high-entity-density prompts (those had historically higher halluc rates).

kai: eval-bot ran a dry-run on our 3k prompt slice — overall embed-similarity delta was +0.2% (good) but a small uptick in hallucination proxy on long-context prompts (0.9% -> 1.6%) — that crosses the gate in the current config.

maya: thanks — that's exactly why I'm running 5% smoke. if that drift persists we should consider either lowering reservoir weight for long-context or tightening the hallucination gate to 0.013 for staged rollout.

rachel: also double-check the reranker thresholds — some of our short-turn lots show precision fluctuation due to tokenization differences after quant. low-hanging: bump reranker synthetic-norm to reduce false negatives.

eval-bot: dry-run report attached: rerank_top1_delta = -0.004, halluc_proxy_delta = 0.007, 99p_latency_delta = 32ms, sample_count = 3240, long_context_slice_delta = +0.007.

oliver: That dry-run looks okay overall (gates not tripped) but long-context is worrying. can we add an early soft-stop: at 5% traffic if long_context_slice_delta > 0.006 then reduce traffic to 1% and notify?

maya: yep I can add soft-stop. adjusting config now and kicking off. updated: soft_stop_long_context_threshold: 0.006, soft_stop_action: reduce_to_1pct.

sre-bot: deploy-bot: canary started for int4-v3 (5% traffic). reservation: reservoir_size=10000, min_samples=500. watch: #eng-ml.

jd: heads-up for dashboards: add a tiny chart showing long_context_slice_delta over rolling 15m windows and annotate soft-stop threshold.

maya: done — dashboard tile created + alert rule. if we hit soft-stop it will auto-reduce and post reason.

oliver: timeline? maya: monitor for 60m then reconvene. if soft-stop triggers, we iterate on reservoir stratification and reranker norm.

rachel: if we end up falling back to nf4-v2, can we run an automated param-compare job to log token-level divergence so research can triage quickly?

maya: yes — auto-collecting a 1k-diff sample and saving to s3://redwood-int4-canary-diffs/3081234567.tar.gz on fallback.

sre-bot: canary metrics update (15m): sample_count=620, rerank_top1_delta=-0.001, halluc_proxy_delta=0.009, long_context_slice_delta=0.005, 99p_latency_delta=28ms.

kai: looking good so far. I'll keep an eye on long-context slice and run targeted offline tests with longer prefixes.

maya: thanks — will post final status in ~60m. if anything trips ping me @maya :eyes:
